HOMELESS SERVICES ADVISORY COMMITTEE MINUTES
  WEDNESDAY, JANUARY 10, 2024
  200 W. BROADWAY
  BILLIE JEAN KING MAIN LIBRARY, 3:30 PM

Julie Lie, Chair  James Howat, Member
Desiree Rew, Vice Chair  Jeffrey Johnson, Member
Sarah Bedy, Member  Mary Simmons, Member
Pat Chotiswatdi, Member  Susana Sngiem, Member

  FINISHED AGENDA & DRAFT MINUTES

CALL TO ORDER

A regular meeting of the Homeless Services Advisory Committee of the City of Long Beach convened
at 3:34 p.m. at Billie Jean King Library. At the start of this meeting, we did not have Quorum. Quorum
was met as 4:12pm.

Pam arrived at 3:53pm, we have a quorum and begin roll call at 4:12pm.

ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present: Lie, Rew, Bedy, Chotiswatdi, Howat, Johnson, Simmons, Sngiem

Also present: Paul Duncan, Homeless Services Bureau Manager, Stephanie Sosa, Community
Program Specialist, Jennifer Santana, Secretary.

Chair Julie Lie presiding.

REGULAR AGENDA

1.  24-51706  Recommendation to approve the Homeless Services Advisory Committee meeting
  on Wednesday, November 1, 2023, and Wednesday, December 6, 2023.

  A motion was made by Member Sngiem, seconded by Vice Chair Rew, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  6  Lie, Rew, Chotiswatdi, Howat, Johnson, Sngiem
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 3  Bedy, Morquecho, Simmons

2.  24-51707  Recommendation to receive and file all Subcommittee updates.

  Mayor’s Fund Subcommittee Update
  • Member James Howat provided the update.

  Page 1 of 6
   HOMELESS SERVICES ADVISORY COMMITTEE MINUTES
  WEDNESDAY, JANUARY 10, 2024
  200 W. BROADWAY
  BILLIE JEAN KING MAIN LIBRARY, 3:30 PM

  • Fundraising amount for November was $14,000 dollars.
  • There is one pending proposal, but the subcommittee will be speaking to the
  applicant at the next subcommittee meeting.
  • Member Jim stated that he had initial concerns that that a fund is being
  perceived and applied to as an emergency fund. An example would be that if
  a homeless provider had an emergency need, the Mayor’s Fund could help
  fund their gap in funding.
  • As well as the fund is not being used to pilot new innovative substantial
  programming and instead getting applications for backpacks and daily
  material things.
  • Discussion ensued regarding having the subcommittee members to be the
  first to look at the applications, to help speed up the process. The application
  process, the priorities and intended use of the fund and the creation of a
  budget template that could help direct applicants to apply in a more concise
  and complete manner.
  • Paul Duncan, Homeless Services Bureau Manager added that the HSB and
  Health Department are responsible for review and approval of release of
  funds and in doing so, there does lie a higher accountability of the funds.
  • Discussion around what the goals that will be given for 2024 and possibility
  to evaluate yearly on what the priorities are.
  • Public Comment from Eloise, as a recipient of the grant it helped her non-
  profit, GP Blanket of Love get a jump start and amplify her reach. As part of
  the Mayor’s Fund, she was given the opportunity to network with other
  organizations in Long Beach to see what available resources there are and
  potential collaborations could be.
Policy Subcommittee Update
  • Chair Julie Lie provided the update.
  • The committee is working on preparing a budget for safe sleep. This will be
  available to HSAC members to share with council.
  • Policy subcommittee shared possible safe sleep sites; committee members
  recommended providing showers.
  • It should be noted that more individuals die from hypothermia here,
  compared the east coast.
  • Member Sarah Bedy and Chair Julie Lie will meet with Councilmember
  Uranga’s office.
CoC Updates
  • Member Pam Chotiswatdi provided update.
  • The CoC is restructuring their subcommittees to look at different stages of
  homelessness and housing to add to better dialogue within the
  subcommittees.
  • There are two open seats for the CoC Board.
  • The Board voted on a Inactivity Policy that removed participants from the
  match list after a 120 days of no contact.
  • Attendance was also discussed and the importance of attendance by the

  A motion was made by Member Sngiem, seconded by Vice Chair Rew, to

  Yes:  6  Lie, Rew, Chotiswatdi, Howat, Johnson, Sngiem

  Absent: 3  Bedy, Morquecho, Simmons

3.  24-51708  Recommendation to receive and file the Homeless Proclamation Update.

  Paul Duncan, Homeless Services Bureau Manager presented in person.
  • The last presentation to the Council was on December 12th. The next update
  to Council will be on February 6th, this will be the last update as the
  Proclamation is set to come to an end on February 28. Although
  Homelessness will remain a priority within the city.
  • In that update the HSB spoke on various projects like Tiny Homes and its
  status with the State. Community engagement started in November and in
  early December a community meeting was convened on site.
  • He provided an update on the Strategic Plan, the city has hired City Fabrik
  as the lead consultant to support the strategic planning process, they are
  working to bring in a secondary partnership with expertise on system and
  data analysis for creating the plan. Community engagement efforts will begin
  after the PIT Count.
  • Due to increased community engagement, the governance structure for
  citywide coordination on homelessness efforts will need to change after the
  emergency. A new team will be created within the City Manager’s Office. The
  goal is to have the team focus on key areas such as policy within the city,
  coordination, projects across depts, and increase community engagement.
  The team will be allocated withing Homeless Services Bureau but will report
  to Deputy City Manager, Teresa Chandler.
  • The HSB is continuing to build capacity by hiring on the reassignments that
  were interested in homeless services.
  • The encampment resolution program R3 is still in the planning stages.
  • We had over 300 survey responses on safe sleeping programs.
  • Inclement weather shelter operation at the MSC started in December and is
  expected to go on for the next few months.
  • LA County Homeless initiative to discuss needs around capacity and
  coordination. This includes discussions around shelter bed rates, the current
  rate that is being paid has been the same since 2017, not ideal with inflation

  Page 3 of 6
   HOMELESS SERVICES ADVISORY COMMITTEE MINUTES
  WEDNESDAY, JANUARY 10, 2024
  200 W. BROADWAY
  BILLIE JEAN KING MAIN LIBRARY, 3:30 PM

  costs. There is discussion around adjusting this rate in LA County overall.
  Several shelters throughout LA county are having difficulty staying afloat due
  to the current bed rates. The County and City of Los Angeles have been
  discussing how to adjust rates through LAHSA. Average rate is currently at
  $75 per night.
  • The Homeless Memorial took place on December 21st, we had a good
  turnout in honor of those that have passed due to being unsheltered last
  year.
  • There has been an increase in studies and data that show an alarming rate
  of older adults coming into homelessness. This could be due to eviction
  protection ending and rising cost of living.
  • The City of Long Beach is looking at ways to stabilize people within their
  current place of residence. With increases in rent and retirement money not
  being enough it can be challenging for older adults; the use of shadow
  subsidies can help stabilize homes without effecting any other government
  help.
  • HUD has released all their PIT Count numbers, and it is highly likely that that
  the 2024 Count will have even bigger increases in Homelessness.
  • Members had questions regarding the community engagement portion of the
  next strategic plan and centralized data regarding government subsidies.
  • Staff answered.

  A motion was made by Member Sngiem, seconded by Member Howat, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  6  Lie, Rew, Chotiswatdi, Howat, Johnson, Sngiem
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 3  Bedy, Morquecho, Simmons

4.  24-51709  Recommendation to receive and file the Homeless Services Bureau Staff Report.

  Paul Duncan, Homeless Services Bureau Manager, presented.
  • Outreach direct phone number, 562-470-4672(4MSC) is live and taking calls.
  • 399 requests for Outreach
  • 198 newly enrolled people in outreach
  • 364 outreach services provided.
  • 394 first-time visitors to the MSC
  • 3,294 total visits in November
  • 165 average daily visits
  • 1,091 phone calls answered
  • 103 Mobile Access Enrollments
  • 2 Mobile Access Center Services Provided

  Page 4 of 6
   HOMELESS SERVICES ADVISORY COMMITTEE MINUTES
  WEDNESDAY, JANUARY 10, 2024
  200 W. BROADWAY
  BILLIE JEAN KING MAIN LIBRARY, 3:30 PM

For the staffing update
  • Hollie Nunez started 12/18/23 as an Admin Analyst III and will be overseeing
  monitoring and compliance.
  • Nancy Toun has been promoted to CPS II Homeless Court Coordinator.
  • Eric Colbert, Vanessa Solorzano, Sharon DeAnda, Giselle Perez, Katelyn,
  Jaramillo, Francisca Orozco, Sarah Zambrano, Kiara Lacambra, Christina,
  Waddington, and David Castro are currently on reassignment from the
  Communicable Disease Emergency Response Division.
  • Positions that are in recruitment/interview phase: Health Educator II,
  • Counselor II, Administrative Analyst III & II, CPS V (program
  • components coordinator), REACH Mental Health Clinician.
  • Recruitments that will begin in the near future: Outreach Coordinator,
  • Community Program Specialist I, IV & V, Homeless Services Program
  • Officers (2), Encampment Resolution positions.
Operation updates include
  • Inclement weather beds at the MSC have begun through the end of
  December we had activated for a total of 5 nights.
  • The second pet vaccine day hosted at the MSC in partnership with Project
  Street Vet. Staff are working towards establishing a regularly scheduled
  event to provide no cost vaccines.
  • The second phone line has been answering calls at the MSC, this has
  expanded capacity for answering calls at the MSC.
  • Encampment Resolution Fund, Round 2 is staffing up with the goal to launch
  the initial sheltering efforts in early 2024.
  • Three project-based sites have begun the application and lease-up process
  over the past month.
  • Staff is continuing to work in developing a regional plan for the next round of
  HHAP 5.
  • Initial planning and surveying to develop an ERF Round 3 proposal.
  • Construction is beginning on the Youth Navigation Center starting this
  month.
  • April Park Foundation is being recommended for award to City Council to
  operate the youth beds at the navigation center.
  • Transition of PHK at 1725 Long Beach Blvd.
  • Illumination foundation has notified the city that it does not intend to renew its
  contract as a service provider at the site.
  • The operation of the site is currently being RFP’ed to identify a new nonprofit
  service provider.
  • Efforts are currently underway to put in place interim operations between
  February and April.

A motion was made by Member Howat, seconded by Member Johnson, to
approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

5.  24-51710  Recommendation to discuss and receive and file the Chair and Vice Chair Report.

  • Vice-chair Desiree reported that she attended the State of the City on
  1/9/2024 and was proud to hear all the amazing work Homeless Services is
  doing and that Paul also was recognized for the work he and have
  completed in the last year.
  • She also is working on getting personnel from Library Services to present.
  • Chair Julie Lie also met the new Police Oversight Commissioner Francine
  Kerridge and she hopes to have her also present to the Committee.
